title: Cocycle and identity laws for normalized ringed-topos derived composition
statement:
Let $X_0\xrightarrow f X_1\xrightarrow g X_2\xrightarrow h X_3$ be morphisms of ringed topoi presented by small sites, with structural maps between sheaves of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $R_f=Rf_*$, and similarly for the other morphisms. Let $\kappa_{g,f}:R_{gf}\xrightarrow{\sim}R_gR_f$ be the K-injective normalized comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. Then, suppressing functor associators,
$$(R_h\kappa_{g,f})\circ\kappa_{h,gf}=(\kappa_{h,g}R_f)\circ\kappa_{hg,f}.$$
The identity comparisons $\epsilon_X:R_{\mathrm{id}_X}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$ are induced by termwise identity direct image, and satisfy
$$(\epsilon_{X_1}R_f)\circ\kappa_{\mathrm{id}_{X_1},f}=1_{R_f},\qquad(R_f\epsilon_{X_0})\circ\kappa_{f,\mathrm{id}_{X_0}}=1_{R_f}.$$
These laws also apply when one or more morphisms are coefficient changes on the identity underlying topos.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; associativity and identity normalization extracted by the total-derived universal property

proof.text: At $Q_0I$ for K-injective $I$, choose $j:f_*I\to J$, $k:g_*J\to K$, $t:g_*f_*I\to T$ using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Apply [lem-pur-ringed-triple-resolution-formulas]: in its common source and target coordinates, the two cocycle paths are $Q_3(h_*u)Q_3(h_*t)$ and $Q_3(h_*k)Q_3(h_*g_*j)$, with $ut\simeq kg_*j$. The additive module direct image of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism] preserves this homotopy: applying $h_*$ to $ut-kg_*j=ds+sd$ gives the same equation for $h_*s$. Functoriality of $Q_3$ therefore identifies the two paths.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; common-resolution assembly using derived.tex Tag 070Y

proof.text: For an arbitrary complex $M$ choose $a:M\to I$ as in [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Write the two natural paths as $\alpha,\beta$ and their source and target functors as $S,T$. Naturality gives $T(Q_0a)\alpha_{Q_0M}=\alpha_{Q_0I}S(Q_0a)$ and the same equation for $\beta$. Since $Q_0a$ is invertible and Step 1 gives $\alpha_{Q_0I}=\beta_{Q_0I}$, cancel $T(Q_0a)$ to obtain equality at $Q_0M$. Every derived object is represented by a complex. The canonical change-of-resolution formulas in [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation] ensure that the coordinates used in Step 1 are the specified ones.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; common-resolution assembly using derived.tex Tag 070Y

proof.text: For termwise identity, [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] says its derived unit $\eta_N:QN\to R_{\mathrm{id}}(QN)$ is invertible for every complex. Thus $\epsilon_{QN}=\eta_N^{-1}$ is the induced natural identity comparison. For a resolution $a:N\to I$, naturality of $\eta$ gives $\eta_I Qa=R_{\mathrm{id}}(Qa)\eta_N$, so $\epsilon_{QN}=(Qa)^{-1}c_a$ with $c_a=\eta_I^{-1}R_{\mathrm{id}}(Qa)$. This also proves independence of $a$, naturality for every derived morphism, and $\epsilon_{QI}=c_{1_I}$ in resolution coordinates. For K-injective $I$ choose $j:f_*I\to J$. The normalization of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] with $g=\mathrm{id}$ represents $\kappa_{\mathrm{id},f}$ by $Q_1j$, while the new identity formula represents $\epsilon_{X_1,Q_1(f_*I)}$ by $(Q_1j)^{-1}$; their composite is $1$. For $\kappa_{f,\mathrm{id}}$, use the identity resolution $I\to I$ of the identity direct image. Its representative is $f_*1_I$, and $R_f(\epsilon_{X_0,Q_0I})$ is the identity in these coordinates by the same identity formula. Their composite is again $1$. The naturality and cancellation equations of Step 2 give both unit laws at every derived object.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor, (3)-(4); Tag 070Y, lemma-K-injective-defined; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0D6E normalization for the two unit cancellations

proof.text: A coefficient change on the identity underlying topos is a ringed-topos morphism whose module direct image is restriction of scalars along the structural ring map [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Every resolution above is in the module category for the ring at that vertex. The preceding arguments apply to these morphisms as well: none requires flatness of the structural map or preservation of K-injectives.

split_report.summary: Deliberate human-requested re-split: old Steps 1-4 become a substantial statement-only unsplit common-resolution formula node. The parent keeps homotopy preservation, explicit naturality cancellation, construction of the identity comparison, both unit cancellations and coefficient changes. Existing exact-functor computation replaces an unnecessary proposed identity leaf. Statement unchanged; 1 new node; no Lean changed. Original arguments and their responsibility map are retained in the report.
split_report.blueprint: fix-prop-adjunctions: ordinary derived adjunction (proof Step 1) and natural, unital, associative ordinary composition (proof Step 3), via lem-pur-completed-coefficient-pushforward-comparison.

tool_uses.why: Small ringed-site K-injective resolution existence; a resolution tool, not a replacement of the mate-unit route.
The Hom bijection into K-injectives detects the chain homotopy needed for the common-resolution calculation.
The arbitrary-derived-morphism and change-of-resolution formulas compute the whiskered comparison; the mate unit does not supply these resolution formulas.
The existing normalized ordinary unbounded ringed-topos composition theorem is the input comparison whose coherence is proved here.
Definition of ringed-topos morphism and its additive module direct image, including coefficient restriction.
Generic exact-functor computation makes the derived identity unit invertible on every complex; supplies the identity normalization without inventing an elementary new node.
